assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square original card portrait for the Moss & Ember painted fantasy game
Primary request: An original portrait of the Coppershade Flock, exactly six small river-workshop gliders.
Scene/backdrop: A softly blurred canal-side workshop at late afternoon, with copper roof reflections, timber rafters, and a little drifting river mist.
Subject: Exactly six distinct, small airborne river gliders in a close group. Design them as a new feathered river-swift species with streamlined warm-gray bodies, softly crested pale faces, small dark amber eyes, long tapered tails, and broad swept feather-sails that shimmer copper where the light passes through. Their feathered wings should feel natural and flexible, never built as machinery or shaped like a bat. They glide in a loose looping formation above the canal, trading a few tiny sparks near a pile of quiet workshop offcuts. Keep each face and wing silhouette visible, and make all six countable at thumbnail size.
Style/medium: Original hand-painted fantasy card illustration with softly sculpted forms, controlled brushwork, matte feather and copper surfaces, clean readable silhouettes, and the warm atmospheric finish of the existing original card art.
Composition/framing: Tight square group portrait with exactly six gliders filling the central area; show complete heads, bodies, and distinct swept wing shapes, with enough space between forms for small card-thumbnail readability.
Lighting/mood: Warm forge light glancing off the river through cool workshop mist; lively, nimble, and curious.
Color palette: Burnished copper wing highlights, warm gray and dark russet bodies, muted teal water, amber spark pinpoints, soft timber browns.
Materials/textures: Fine layered feathers, subtle copper-shimmer wing edges, worn timber, canal reflections, painted mist.
Text (verbatim): None.
Constraints: Exactly six original gliders; original design, no copied commercial-game art or character; no symbols, captions, letters, UI, frame, border, watermark, or logo.
Avoid: Bats, owls, moths, amphibians, armor, humanoid forms, visible machinery, gears, propellers, weapons, extra animals, photorealism, glossy 3D plastic, flat vector art, text.
